questions.question: Describe the national flag and explain what its design is understood to mean.
questions.expected_answer: The national flag was designed by Frederick Brownell, the State Herald, and first flown on the twenty-seventh of April 1994. It has six colours, chilli red, white, green, gold, black and blue, but no official meaning for each colour. Its main design is a horizontal Y shape in which two bands come together and flow into one, usually understood to show different parts of society coming together and moving forward in unity. It must be treated with respect, for example never touching the ground.

questions.question: Describe the coat of arms and explain the meaning of four of its parts.
questions.expected_answer: The coat of arms was launched on the twenty-seventh of April 2000. The motto, in the /Xam San language, means diverse people unite. The shield shows two figures from the Linton Stone rock painting greeting each other, a sign of unity. The spear and knobkierie lying down represent peace and authority. The protea represents beauty, the elephant tusks wisdom and strength, the wheat growth, the secretary bird protection and the rising sun a new beginning.

questions.question: Explain how the national anthem was created and why it shows reconciliation.
questions.expected_answer: The anthem combines Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika, composed by Enoch Sontonga in 1897 and sung by the liberation movement, and Die Stem van Suid-Afrika, written by C. J. Langenhoven and used as the anthem of the old South Africa. Both were sung from 1994, and in 1997 a shortened combined version became the single anthem, using isiXhosa, isiZulu, Sesotho, Afrikaans and English. Joining songs from different sides of the divided past shows reconciliation and unity.
